title: Needlestick injury
stem: Cubicle 2, 03:00. Nurse Ho, 32, was stuck 40 minutes ago by a hollow needle after taking blood from a ward patient. She is upset. Take a history, assess the risk and counsel her.

review.text: PEP duration. Your notes say 'PEP for 28 weeks'. It is 28 days.

PEP when the source has an undetectable viral load. Your second scenario gives PEP to a source who is HIV-positive on treatment with an undetectable load. BHIVA/BASHH 2021 advise against PEP then; discuss with the on-call infectious disease physician.
HBIG dose. Your notes give 0.06 mL/kg, the US dose. UK practice gives 500 IU.

notes:
Checked against the Hong Kong Scientific Committee on AIDS and STI / Centre for Health Protection recommendations on management of occupational exposure to HBV, HCV and HIV, the UK BHIVA/BASHH PEP guideline (2021), and UKHSA guidance.

Immediate: encourage bleeding, wash with soap and running water; do not scrub or suck; irrigate mucosa.

Risk per percutaneous exposure to a positive source: HBV about 6–30% (if non-immune; depends on HBeAg), HCV about 1.8% (lower in recent series, ~0.2–0.5%), HIV about 0.3%. Higher with hollow-bore needles, deep injury, visible blood, a needle from a vein or artery, and high source viral load.

HBV: check the recipient's vaccination and anti-HBs; known responder (≥10 mIU/mL) needs nothing; non-responder or unknown with a positive source needs HBIG plus vaccine. HCV: no PEP; baseline and follow-up testing (HCV RNA at 6 weeks, antibody at 12–24 weeks). HIV PEP: start as soon as possible, ideally within hours, not after 72 hours, for 28 days. UK BHIVA/BASHH 2021 advise against PEP if the source is on ART with a confirmed undetectable viral load; HK guidance takes a similar risk-based approach — discuss with the on-call infectious disease physician.

Your notes: 'PEP for 28 weeks' should be 28 days; your second scenario recommends PEP when the source is HIV-positive with an undetectable viral load, which current UK guidance does not; HBIG 0.06 mL/kg is the US dose (UK uses 500 IU). The rest matches.

This station: source is known HCV-positive, HIV and HBV unknown; the source consents to testing.

steps.label: History
steps.hint: Event, first aid, recipient status, source status.

Event.r: Forty minutes ago. I was recapping — I know, I shouldn't — and it went into my left index finger.

Event.t: What kind of needle? Was there blood in it?
Event.r: A hollow blood-taking needle, just used in a vein. There was blood in it.
Event.mark: Asks needle type and visible blood (hollow-bore, from a vein)

Event.t: How deep? Were you wearing gloves?
Event.r: Quite deep, it bled. Gloves on.

Event.t: What did you do straight after?
Event.r: I squeezed it and washed it with alcohol swabs.

You.t: Hepatitis B vaccination and antibody level?
You.r: Three doses in nursing school. My antibody was checked once — 150.
You.mark: Asks HBV vaccination and antibody response

You.t: Any illness, medicines, pregnancy or breastfeeding?
You.r: Healthy. Not pregnant. On the pill.
You.mark: Asks pregnancy and medical history (affects PEP)

Source.t: What do we know about the patient?
Source.r: A 50-year-old man with hepatitis C. Past drug use. HIV status unknown.
Source.mark: Asks what is known about the source

steps.label: Management
steps.hint: Wash now; bloods; source testing with consent; HBV immune; HIV risk assessment; follow-up; incident report.

opts.t: Wash again with soap and running water; no scrubbing or antiseptic
Baseline bloods from her: HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HCV, HIV, with consent; store serum
Ask the ward to consent and test the source for HIV, HBV, HCV RNA urgently
opts.mark: Source testing with the source's consent

opts.t: Discuss HIV PEP now with the ID physician while the source result is awaited
opts.mark: Considers HIV PEP promptly, pending source results

opts.t: Occupational health follow-up; incident report; off shift tonight
opts.mark: Occupational health, incident report, off duty

opts.r: She is a known responder (anti-HBs 150): no HBV prophylaxis needed.

opts.t: Start treatment for hepatitis C immediately as PEP
opts.r: There is no HCV PEP; test and follow up, treat early if she seroconverts.

steps.label: Counsel Nurse Ho
steps.hint: Risks in numbers, plan, precautions, support.

turns.line: Am I going to get hepatitis C? Or HIV?

opts.t: The risk is low. For hepatitis C it's about 1 in 50 or less; for HIV, if he had it, about 1 in 300. You're protected against hepatitis B. We'll test him and you, and we have treatments if anything shows up.

turns.line: What do I do until the results come back?

opts.t: Use condoms, don't donate blood, organs or breast milk until follow-up is clear, and come to occupational health tomorrow. The tests are at 6 weeks and 3–6 months.
opts.r: And can I tell my husband?

turns.line: I feel so stupid for recapping.

opts.t: These injuries happen to many of us. The important thing is you came straight away. Sister Yu will cover the rest of your shift.
opts.mark: Supports without blame and arranges cover

qs.q: HIV transmission risk after a percutaneous injury from an HIV-positive source?
Latest time to start HIV PEP?
PEP when the source is on ART with an undetectable viral load (BHIVA/BASHH 2021)?

badge.name: Sharp Mind
badge.flavor: Wash, test both sides, PEP by risk, follow up, never recap.

options: Encourage bleeding; wash with soap and water
Suck the wound to remove the blood
Scrub hard with alcohol and dilute bleach solution
Apply a tourniquet above the wound
cards.why: Avoid scrubbing and antiseptics that damage skin.

cards.q: HCV transmission after a positive-source needlestick is about…
Known HBV vaccine responder after a needlestick: HBV prophylaxis?

options: As soon as possible, within 72 hours
Only once the source is confirmed HIV-positive

cards.q: Which increases HIV risk in a needlestick?
options: A solid suture needle through a double glove
Wearing a single pair of thin latex gloves
cards.why: Also deep injury and high source viral load.
Your notes say 28 weeks — a typo.
